label: HMRC update · 10 November 2026
title: Start your 2025 to 2026 tax return now: five things to check before 31 January
summary: Around 5 million people leave their tax return until January. Here are the points worth checking now, including the Winter Fuel Payment, Child Benefit and crypto gains.
body:
HMRC is encouraging people not to wait until January. Around 12 million people are expected to file a tax return each year, and around 5 million often leave it until January. The deadline to file the 2025 to 2026 return online and pay any tax owed is 31 January 2027.

Filing early does not mean paying early

If you file now, you still do not have to pay until 31 January. What you get is the exact figure, and time to plan for it.

Five things to check this year

  • PAYE coding. If you have PAYE income and file online before 30 December, you may be able to have tax owed collected through your tax code instead of paying it in one go.
  • Winter Fuel Payment. If you received the 2025 Winter Fuel Payment and your total income is over £35,000, it is paid back through your Self Assessment bill. HMRC pre-fills it where it can, but you should check it and add it if it is missing.
  • High Income Child Benefit Charge. Child Benefit details are now pre-filled on the online return for people who pay the charge through Self Assessment. Some people can now pay the charge monthly through their tax code instead.
  • Crypto. Gains on cryptoassets above the £3,000 tax-free allowance are subject to Capital Gains Tax and must go on the return.
  • Making Tax Digital. If you have already joined MTD for Income Tax, you still file your 2025 to 2026 return in the usual way by 31 January 2027.

What I would do

  • Gather your P60, bank interest, dividend vouchers, rental figures and business records now.
  • Find your Unique Taxpayer Reference in the HMRC app or a past letter.
  • If you are not sure whether you need to file, use the Self Assessment checker on GOV.UK, or ask us.

sources.title: Stay on top of your finances, start your Self Assessment today (GOV.UK, 10 November 2026)
